lesson.title: Sealed But Not Silent: Understanding Closed Systems
lesson.summary: A closed system can exchange energy with its surroundings but not matter, so its total mass stays constant even as heat flows freely in or out.
lesson.body:
A closed system is one whose boundary allows energy, such as heat or work, to cross freely, while blocking matter from entering or leaving entirely. Whatever substance is inside stays inside, in exactly the same amount, for as long as the system remains closed.

Picture a tightly sealed glass bottle containing a reaction mixture, placed in a warm water bath. The glass walls conduct heat readily, so the contents warm up as the surrounding water heats them, meaning energy is clearly crossing the boundary. But the sealed cap prevents any gas or liquid inside from escaping, and prevents anything from the water bath outside from getting in, so the total amount of substance inside the bottle stays exactly the same throughout, even though its temperature, and its internal energy, are changing the whole time.

It helps to compare this directly to the open pot of boiling water from the previous chapter. Take that same pot, on the same burner, and simply put a tight fitting lid on it. Now, steam that would have escaped instead condenses on the underside of the lid and drips back down into the pot rather than leaving the system, so the total mass inside stays essentially constant even though heat is still flowing in from the burner just as freely as before. Swapping an open boundary for a closed one changes the category of the exact same physical setup, without changing anything about the heat source itself.

This is also why many classic gas law demonstrations, such as a fixed amount of gas trapped in a syringe with a sealed tip, or gas confined in a rigid sealed container placed over a heat source, are treated as closed systems: the amount of gas present is fixed, but the container is not thermally isolated, so temperature changes still affect the trapped gas as heat crosses the boundary. The key point to keep straight is that closed refers specifically to matter being blocked, not to energy: a closed system is not thermally sealed off at all, it is simply a fixed amount of material whose energy remains free to change.
